newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen end barely higher on stock weakness.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen end barely higher on stock weakness.

text.p: The key December three-month euroyen futures contract ended slightly higher on Thursday due to weakness in Tokyo share prices, traders said.
"December was bought as share prices remained weak in the afternoon," a brokerage house trader said.
"The upside was limited, however, as selling pressure was strong at 98.94 and 98.95," he added.
Although the figures for Tokyo department store sales in April came out weaker than expected, there was not much impact on euroyen futures, a city bank trader said.

"Most players had expected Tokyo department store sales in April to have fallen by less than 10 percent year-on-year. Even though the actual figure showed a sharper than expected fall, there was little effect on euroyen futures," he said.
Sales at department stores in Tokyo fell 14.4 percent in April from a year earlier to 166.1 billion yen, the Japan Department Stores' Association said on Thursday.
The Bank of Japan refrained from conducting its regular 0020 GMT operation this morning. The money market had a projected fund shortage of 10 billion yen going into the day.
The weighted average of the key overnight call rate is likely to be 0.43 percent on Thursday, down from Wednesday's weighted average of 0.45 percent, traders said.
The key overnight call rate fell because banks had been able to pile up their necessary reserves smoothly during the current bank reserves reporting period, traders said.
The market will be watching the BOJ's money market stance on Friday, the first day of a new reporting period, they said.
About 70 billion yen worth of the key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.57 percent while 10 billion yen worth of three-month CDs were issued at 0.56 percent, traders said.
The decline in the key three-month CD rate from 0.58 percent on Wednesday is probably due to a fall in the key overnight call rate, a trader for another city bank said.

The market may feel that the key short-term rate will not rise sharply above 0.50 percent even when a new bank reserve reporting period starts, and this is putting downward pressure on the three-month CD rate, the trader said.
